title: The owner is a team attribute and only an admin can take ownership
context: The owner used to be the one player holding the OWNER role, enforced by a partial unique index per team. Transferring ownership was two player writes (promote the target, demote the outgoing owner) with a compensating write when the second failed, so a failure between them could leave a team with two owners or none, and every owner check had to read the caller's role. Google Drive requires the recipient of an ownership transfer to be an editor first, and the original owner then becomes an editor (https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2494892).
decision: The owner is Team.ownerPlayerId. Player roles are MEMBER and ADMIN, and the owner is always an ADMIN. Transfer is one conditional team write that sets ownerPlayerId only while it still equals the caller's player; the loser of a race gets NOT_TEAM_OWNER. Only a joined ADMIN may receive ownership, and the previous owner stays an ADMIN. Owner-only checks read the team, not the caller's role. This replaces ADR-0043's definition of the owner as the member holding the OWNER role; the rest of that decision stands.

alternatives.option: Keep OWNER as a player role and make transfer a transaction over the two player writes
alternatives.reason: It keeps the unique index and the role check on every owner test, and the owner remains derived from two rows that must agree; a single team field cannot disagree with itself.

alternatives.option: Allow any joined member as the target and promote them to ADMIN in the same transfer
alternatives.reason: It adds a second write to the transfer, which is the non-atomic pair this decision removes, and lets the owner grant admin rights as a side effect of a handover.

consequences: Transfer is atomic, and a team always has exactly one owner, always an ADMIN.
A role change or removal that targets the team's ownerPlayerId is refused with TARGET_IS_OWNER, so the owner stays an ADMIN until ownership moves.
A residual race remains: a target demoted between the read and the transfer write becomes the owner holding the MEMBER role. The write is conditional on the owner only, not on the target's role.
Existing data needs a one-time migration that sets ownerPlayerId from the OWNER player, demotes that player to ADMIN and drops the owner unique index; scripts/migrate-team-owner.js does this.
revisitTriggers: The residual demotion race is observed in practice, or transfer must also guard the target's role in the same write.
Ownership transfer changes to require the recipient's acceptance.
